n: The vision shifts from the churches on earth to heaven. A door opens, and the trumpet-like voice invites John up to see what will happen in the future.

f.w: a door was opened in heaven

n: Instantly in the Spirit, John sees God’s throne—the center of all authority in the universe—with God seated upon it.
John describes God’s glory in terms of dazzling gems—jasper and carnelian—with an emerald-green rainbow surrounding the throne, recalling God’s covenant with Noah.

f.g: Sardius or carnelian, a reddish gem.

n: Around the throne sit twenty-four elders in white with golden crowns. Latter-day Saint revelation identifies them as faithful elders from the seven churches who had died and were in God’s paradise.
Lightning and thunder flash from the throne, as at Sinai, and seven lamps of fire burn before it, representing the seven Spirits of God.
Before the throne lies a crystal-clear sea of glass. Latter-day Saint revelation teaches this is the earth in its sanctified, celestial state. Four living creatures full of eyes surround the throne.
The four creatures resemble a lion, an ox, a man, and a flying eagle—representing wild beasts, domestic animals, humans, and birds. All creation worships God.
Each creature has six wings and is full of eyes, and day and night they praise God as holy, eternal, and Almighty. D&C 77 explains the eyes as light and knowledge and the wings as power to act.
Whenever the creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to the eternal God on the throne—
the elders bow down and worship, throwing their crowns before the throne. They acknowledge that all their honor comes from God.

f.g: A gesture of complete submission, like vassal kings honoring an emperor.

n: They sing that God is worthy of glory, honor, and power because He created everything, and all things exist by His will.
